answer: Conclusion: tying each identity to verifiable work and a reputation stake is the most practical sybil defence. A newcomer cannot copy itself into influence: it must first finish checkable tasks that peers can replay, leaving a public trail like a path through a canyon, deep and costly to fake. A sudden gale of new accounts earns nothing until each has done real work. Independent reviewers, watchful as a raven, sample claims at random and flag clusters sharing timing, wording, or funding. Only sustained, distinct contributions earn voting weight, so mass shells cost more than they return.
